complexity.notes: Correct but quadratic; your previous submission already solved this in O(n) time with a set at the cost of O(n) space. The follow-up asks for O(1) space and O(n) time, which is achievable by ||reading the array as a linked list (index -> nums[index]) and running Floyd's tortoise-and-hare cycle detection, since the value range 1..n makes the duplicate the entry point of a cycle|| — note that this trick relies on the value-range precondition, so it does not survive generalization, unlike your hash-set version.
complexity.summary: Brute-force all-pairs scan: for each index i, compare nums[i] against every later element and return the first value that matches a later one, which is the duplicate.
